A1.justification: The PDFs clearly describe successive versions of the same work, despite renaming CUT to AnomalyAny, and all supplied pages are readable. However, v1 includes Appendix A.1–A.6, whereas v2 references supplementary implementation details, user-study results, and additional examples that are absent from the supplied PDF. These gaps limit comparison of that material.

before.justification: v1 reports original anomaly-generation examples, few-shot and full-shot detection experiments, supervision ablations, and a 20-participant user study in Appendix A.3.

after.justification: v2 reports quantitative generation-quality and diversity results, qualitative refinement ablations, and retained one-shot detection results. Retained original results still qualify.

M1.justification: Beyond renaming, v2 Section 4.3 introduces detailed GPT-4-generated descriptions, CLIP image-text and prompt-alignment losses, and joint optimization of latent representations and prompt embeddings during the final 30 steps. Section 4.1 also introduces explicit replacement of latent content outside optional masks. The original normal-image conditioning, attention optimization, and localization-aware scheduler remain recognizable.

E1.justification: Both versions retain MVTec AD, VisA, and qualitative generation using web images. However, v1 Figure 12 includes additional cup, vase, and phone examples; v2 defers further examples to an unavailable supplement, so retention of this wider qualitative object coverage cannot be verified. The reduction in reported shot counts is a protocol change.

E2.justification: v1 Table 2 evaluates full-shot comparators UniAD, SimpleNet, DiAD, and AnomalyGPT; that comparison is absent from supplied v2, eliminating its distinct full-shot comparator coverage. The five one-shot detection baselines and four generator-substitution baselines remain unchanged. v2's new generation-quality table evaluates the already-used NSA, RealNet, and AnomalyDiffusion methods.

E3.justification: Reported detection evaluation narrows from 1-, 2-, 4-, and full-shot settings to one-shot. v2 adds Inception Score and IC-LPIPS evaluation and controls for prompt-refinement ablations. It also states 100 SD inference steps, versus 200 in v1 Appendix A.1; this establishes a reported setting revision, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Figures 8–10 add comparisons of short versus detailed prompts, attention versus prompt guidance, and individual refinement-loss terms. Figure 3 also gains a prompt-refinement ablation. Conversely, v1 Table 4's quantitative image-only versus pixel-only supervision analysis is absent from supplied v2. The generator-substitution experiment remains in Table 3.

E5.justification: The retained one-shot comparisons preserve five-run reporting and identical uncertainty values. However, v2 no longer explicitly identifies the reported variability as standard deviation or supplies the random-seed description found in v1 Section 5.1 and appendix captions. No increase in runs or new statistical testing is established.

E6.justification: v2 Table 1 adds generation results, including average IS/IC-LPIPS of 2.02/0.33 for AnomalyAny versus 1.80/0.32 for AnomalyDiffusion. All numerical entries in the retained one-shot detection and generator-substitution tables match v1. The two-shot, four-shot, full-shot, and supervision-ablation results are no longer supplied. These changes do not establish a version-to-version performance gain.

T1.justification: v2 introduces substantive mathematical definitions for background-preserving latent blending and CLIP-guided image/prompt objectives with joint updates in Equations 5 and 10–13. v1's adapted Dice loss and VLAD scoring formulations are absent from supplied v2. The mathematical formulation changes substantially, although neither version provides theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 claims a separate VLAD detector, an adapted Dice loss, and state-of-the-art detection performance spanning few-shot and full-shot settings. v2 replaces these contributions with prompt-guided refinement within an unseen-anomaly generation framework and a more general claim of downstream detection effectiveness. Training-free generation across unseen objects and anomaly types remains central.

C2.justification: v2 explains the ambiguity of short anomaly descriptions and the smaller refinement benefit for unambiguous concepts such as rust. Its conclusion replaces v1's coarse-annotation limitation with limitations of CLIP on lengthy, specialized descriptions and proposes anomalous-image guidance as future work. It also changes the interpretation of unchanged Table 3 results from outperforming AnomalyDiffusion in most metrics to comparable performance.

D1.justification: v1 supplies the detector backbone, training epochs, image size, batch size, optimizer, hardware, optimization thresholds, and model-resource links. Much of this information is unavailable in supplied v2, which defers implementation to its missing supplement. v2 adds the final-30-step refinement schedule and replaces the project-page link with a future code-release statement; actual resource availability cannot be verified locally.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including GPT-4, NNG-Mix, Few-shot Anomaly-Driven Generation, Defect Spectrum, and cross-domain image-generation correspondence. References supporting the omitted detector discussion, including SimpleNet, DiAD, focal loss, and generalized Dice loss, disappear. Research positioning emphasizes unseen-generation limitations more explicitly while retaining the original training-free motivation.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion are substantially rewritten around AnomalyAny. The methodology becomes three generation-focused subsections instead of separate generation and VLAD sections, related-work subsections reverse order, and the experimental narrative shifts toward generation quality and one-shot detection. This is extensive restructuring beyond terminology changes.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 2 is redrawn with the prompt-optimization branch, Figure 3 gains a comparison condition, and Figure 7 transposes and expands existing examples. New generation and ablation displays accompany condensed detection tables; v1's appendix displays are not included in supplied v2.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the generation-focused evidence with quantitative quality/diversity evaluation and targeted refinement ablations. However, its unchanged one-shot scores do not establish downstream benefits from the revised procedure, and important detector and reproducibility information is deferred to an unavailable supplement. These gains and documentation gaps prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
